messages:
jen_support: Heads up — ACME (acct: ACME-KS) was charged 8.5% sales tax on invoice #INV-2026-4821 even though they submitted a KS resale cert last month. Customer opened a support ticket, wants credit + corrected invoice. Can someone triage? :exclamation:

maya_finance: Sorry about that. Can you paste the invoice id + payment method? I can start a provisional credit while we investigate. :pray:

jen_support: Invoice: INV-2026-4821, payment via card ending 4242, charged on 2026-02-18. Attached the customer's resale cert in the ticket. They bill to: 123 Commerce Rd, Wichita, KS.

sam_irwin: Quick check — was the invoice generated from the billing address or PO entity? We've seen cases where card BIN country or Stripe address fallback causes jurisdiction to flip.

jen_support: It was generated from the account billing address (KS). No PO. Customer mentioned they updated the account address last week.

tax_ops: I pulled the invoice metadata: tax_jurisdiction=MA, tax_rate=0.085, tax_provider=stripe_tax. Looks like the tax lookup returned MA. That explains the 8.5% amount.

jen_support: How would MA get selected if the account address is KS? 

anna_engineer: Possible repro path we've seen: 1) user updates billing address, 2) webhook sync to billing service fails, 3) next invoice creation falls back to payment method address (card). If card BIN is issued in MA or payment provider returned MA as shipping/billing country, stripe_tax can choose MA.

anna_engineer: Repro curl to check invoice creation payload we log: ```
POST /v1/invoices 
{
  "customer": "cus_ABC123",
  "billing_address": {"line1":"123 Commerce Rd","region":"KS","country":"US"},
  "payment_method": "pm_1xxxxx"
}
```

anna_engineer: Check our logs for the outbound tax lookup call to Stripe: we send customer address and payment method; if payment method country overwrites or is used by Stripe, it can affect jurisdiction.

maya_finance: For immediate remediation: we can issue a credit note and reissue a corrected invoice zeroing tax. Steps I will take after confirmation: 1) create credit note for INV-2026-4821 2) refund the tax portion to the card 3) create new invoice INV-2026-4821-R1 with proper tax=0 and mark as paid.

liam_ops: If we refund to card, ensure PCI refund tied to original charge id. Finance will need the charge id and refund reason. Also flag for review so we don't auto-apply tax again on retry.

jen_support: Charge id: ch_1H2k3l4m5n. Customer accepts refund. Please proceed, @maya_finance.

maya_finance: Starting provisional credit now. Posting steps and ETA in ticket. ETA for refund post: 3-5 business days.

sam_irwin: Engineering action item: add a check in invoice creation that validates tax_jurisdiction == account.billing_region unless explicit override exists. If mismatch, log and halt creation pending manual review. We have a couple similar incidents in the last month — low-weight but high-impact.

anna_engineer: Agreed. I'll open a PR to add a sanity check and an extra telemetry event when tax provider returns inconsistent jurisdiction. Quick mitigation: set priority to ensure webhook/address-sync retries are less likely to race invoice creation.

tax_ops: Also adding a rule in tax mapping to prefer customer.billing_address over payment_method.country when both present. That reduces BIN-induced flips.

maya_finance: Credit issued (credit_note_CN-2026-0098) and refund started to ch_1H2k3l4m5n. Created replacement invoice INV-2026-4821-R1 with tax = 0. Customer notified.

jen_support: Thanks team — I'll mark the Zendesk ticket as escalated-resolved pending refund clearance. Please ping if any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

liam_ops: Leaving a follow-up task in #eng-bugs to verify no other invoices affected. Sam/Anna to coordinate.

sam_irwin: Will scan invoices in the last 30 days for tax_jurisdiction != billing_region and report findings by EOD.

tax_ops: Noted. Also will reach out to Stripe to confirm how payment_method.country is being used in their tax calculations for our integration.

jen_support: Closing loop here — customer replied: "Thanks, refund ETA works for us. Please ensure future invoices are tax-exempt." :smile:
